notes: Session 14 recap. We picked up right where we left off, in the flooded cellar under the Silt Street chandlery. Mira waded ahead with the lantern and found the drain grate, but it was rusted shut, so Brakka braced her boots on the wall and wrenched it open on the second try. Behind it was the smugglers' tunnel. Tovin went first because he's the quietest, and he spotted the tripwire about ten feet in; he disarmed it with a hairpin and some swearing. The tunnel came out in a warehouse where four smugglers were counting coin. Ilse walked straight in and told them we were from the Harbour Guild and here for the monthly cut. Three of them bought it. The fourth didn't, went for his crossbow, and Brakka put him through a crate. After that the others were very cooperative. We tied them up and Mira patched the one Brakka hit, because she's soft like that. In the ledger Tovin found the name of the buyer, a Lady Voss, which nobody at the table has heard of yet. We ended the night at the Crooked Kettle where Ilse lost eleven silver at dice.

ok so long one tonight. road to Harrowmere. first day nothing much, Pip foraged and found a patch of wild onions so dinner was good. second day the bridge over the Dunn was out, washed away, so Oskar swam across with a rope and we ferried the gear over in the cart tarp. took all afternoon. that night wolves circled the camp. Fen kept the fire high and Nereth scared them off with a thunderclap spell, big boom, wolves gone. third day we reached Harrowmere and the gate sergeant wouldnt let us in without papers. Wick tried to fast talk him and got nowhere, so Jesk just showed him the Duke's ring and he waved us through. in town Nereth went to the mages hall and spent the evening copying spells from their library, Pip went to the market and sold the wolf pelts from last week. Oskar got into an arm wrestling contest at the tavern and won four rounds before losing to a half orc blacksmith.

The Siege of Corran's Ford, night two.

Dusk: the enemy brought up a ram. Captain Aldric (NPC) was wounded early, so Jesk took command of the east wall. She reorganized the archers into two ranks and they drove back the first assault.

Midnight: sappers were heard under the north tower. Esk put her ear to the stone, figured out roughly where they were digging, and collapsed their tunnel with an earth spell. Nobody got out.

The small hours: Hadrik and Brakka held the breach at the gatehouse when the ram finally broke through. They were outnumbered maybe eight to one and should have died, honestly. Hadrik took a spear through the shoulder and kept fighting.

Dawn: Selma spent the morning in the infirmary treating wounded, including Hadrik, whose shoulder she set and stitched. The enemy pulled back at sunrise. Afterwards the survivors from the east wall came to find Jesk and thank her; a couple of them asked if she'd be staying on as captain. She said no, but you could tell she thought about it. The enemy banners were still on the far ridge at the end of the session.

Dear diary (Kip's player writing this, lol). So the party split up in the city. Me (Kip) and Tamsin went to case the bank. Tamsin climbed up to the roof and counted the guards changing shifts, I chatted up a teller and learned the vault is opened at 9 sharp every morning. Meanwhile Aurel and Grell went to the temple to ask about the plague. Aurel prayed with the sick for hours, and the high priestess was impressed enough to let him read the temple's plague records, where he found out it started at the tannery. Grell got bored and went and threatened the tanner, who confessed the new dye came from a 'wizard with green hands'. We regrouped at the inn. Nobody could agree on whether to rob the bank or chase the wizard so we did neither and went to bed, and next week we're chasing the wizard. Tamsin won a knife-throwing contest at the inn before bed though, which was cool.

Downtime month. Wren spent the whole month at the forge in Irongate. She made a longsword for Hadrik, reworked her own armor, and the smith offered her an apprenticeship which she accepted. Liora took a residency at the Gilded Lark playing three nights a week; by the end of the month people were requesting her song about the siege. Tovin worked as a clerk at the Harbour Guild to get access to their records, and he found three shipments that match the Voss ledger. He also got caught reading a sealed file once and had to talk his way out of it, which he did, barely. Selma volunteered at the leper house outside the walls, treating patients every day. Grell did nothing productive and got banned from two taverns for brawling. We also spent a chunk of the session just roleplaying the Irongate smith, who has opinions about everything, including Hadrik's grip. Next session we pick back up with the Voss investigation now that we have actual evidence, and Tovin wants to go straight to the magistrate with it.

Big session. The heist on the Voss manor.
We went in during the masquerade. Ilse and Wick went through the front door in disguise, Ilse as a visiting countess, Wick as her servant. Ilse danced with Lord Voss himself and kept him busy for most of an hour while dropping hints about a fake investment. Tovin and Kip came over the garden wall. Kip picked the lock on the study window in about a minute, Tovin found the hidden safe behind a painting and cracked it, got the letters. On the way out a guard dog found them. Kip tried to calm it with a bit of sausage, which did not work at all, and it bit him. Tovin threw a smoke pellet and they got over the wall. Meanwhile inside, a guest recognized Wick from the Harrowmere gate, so Wick created a distraction by knocking over a tower of champagne glasses, and he and Ilse slipped out in the confusion.

Played the dungeon crawl tonight. Room 1: skeletons, easy, Kesh and Brenna smashed them. Room 2: puzzle with the four statues. Juno spent forever on it and finally realised the inscriptions were a calendar and set the statues to the solstice positions. Door opened. Room 3: flooded corridor, Oskar carried Juno across on his shoulders because she can't swim. Room 4: a wight. It drained Brenna badly and she went down; Aurel brought her back with a heal and then turned the wight with his holy symbol and it fled. Room 5: treasure, including a cursed ring that Kesh put on immediately because of course he did. Juno identified the curse afterwards but can't remove it. Next session starts in room 6. We also spent a while arguing about splitting the loot, since Kesh wants the cursed ring's gold value counted against his share and nobody else agrees. Brenna is still at half her max HP from the drain, so Aurel promised to pray over her in the morning before we go on.

Wilderness week. Pim led us up into the Greyteeth and honestly he was amazing, found a pass that isn't on any map. On the second night the snow came in and we'd have frozen if Fen hadn't dug a snow cave for all six of us. Third day a yeti attacked. Rook's hawk spotted it first and gave us a few seconds warning. Hadrik and Brakka fought it off while Mara shot it from a ledge; it fled with three arrows in it. Kip slipped on the ice during the fight and slid about forty feet down a slope, broke his leg. Selma set the leg and splinted it. We had to carry him for two days. On the way down Pim found yeti tracks leading to a cave full of bones and old gear, including a dwarven compass that still works. By the time we got to the lowland village everyone was exhausted and half frozen. The villagers put us up in the mill and the reeve asked a lot of questions about the pass Pim found, because apparently they'd love to trade across it without paying the road toll.

Council session, very talky, which I loved. The three guild heads met at the Mercer's Hall about the tariff war. Ilse opened by flattering the Weavers, then pivoted to accusing the Chandlers of hoarding lamp oil, which put them on the back foot. The Chandler's rep tried to discredit her by bringing up her gambling debts and she laughed it off. Tovin produced the shipping ledgers as proof, and that basically ended it; the Chandlers agreed to drop the tariff. Afterwards Jesk had a private meeting with the Watch captain and convinced him to post guards at the docks. Aurel said a blessing for the new agreement at the end, which was a nice touch. Nobody rolled initiative all night. Grell spent the whole meeting eating the free pastries and glaring at the Chandler rep, which Ilse claims was part of her plan. After the meeting, the Weavers invited the whole party to a dinner next week, and Tovin is suspicious that it's a trap. Probably is.

Naval session. We left port at dawn on the Grey Heron. By noon a pirate cutter was chasing us. Harl, at the wheel, made the call to run into the fog bank, which was risky with the reefs but worked. Inside the fog Nereth cast a gust spell to keep our sails full while the pirates' went slack. We lost them. Then the reefs: Dov went up the mast to call out rocks and Harl threaded us through. In the evening we found a wreck with survivors clinging to it. Oskar and Dov rowed the jolly boat over and pulled off five sailors, one of whom was the Duke's missing nephew. On the way back to the ship the boat nearly capsized and Oskar lost his sword to the sea. We put in at a fishing village overnight to repair the jolly boat and resupply. The Duke's nephew turned out to be insufferable and spent dinner complaining about the food, the bunks, and Oskar's singing, in roughly that order. He did promise us a reward, though, so we're keeping him alive.

The tournament at Highcombe. Day 1 was archery: Mara placed second, beaten only by the Elven champion; her last shot split the previous arrow and the crowd went mad. Day 2 was the melee: Hadrik fought through four opponents and lost the final to Ser Brannic, who is apparently level 12 or something, Hadrik is level 4, it wasn't close but he lasted three rounds which everyone agreed was insane. Day 3 was the joust, which nobody entered. Liora performed at the closing feast and composed a verse about Hadrik's last stand that made Ser Brannic laugh and buy him a drink. Grell lost a lot of money betting on Hadrik. In between events there was a lot of shopping, and Kip spent most of day two trying to get into the noble stands without a ticket, which failed repeatedly and hilariously. The Duke's herald did ask Hadrik to visit the castle next week, so that's a hook for later.

Bit of a weird session, the GM (me) let things go sideways. The party was supposed to investigate the haunted mill. Instead Kip decided to open a pie stall in the market to 'build cover'. He actually rolled really well, the pies sold out, and a food critic NPC I improvised wrote him a glowing review. Meanwhile Saoirse did go to the mill and held a séance, contacted the miller's ghost, who told her about the murder. She was badly shaken by it. Rook tried to help by summoning his hawk to watch the mill overnight but the ghost scared it off. Tamsin spent the day teaching the orphans at the chapel to read, which I also didn't plan for but was very sweet. Next week: the murder. Grell sat in the tavern all day and did nothing, as usual, but he did end up befriending the food critic, which may become relevant. The mill itself is still standing, the ghost is still in it, and the party now knows the miller was killed by someone he trusted.

Long fight tonight, whole session basically. Black Dragon lair. We were level 5, the dragon was CR 14, we were never supposed to fight it, we were supposed to sneak in and steal the egg. Tovin got caught on the way out. What followed: Brakka held the tunnel mouth under the acid breath while Tovin ran past. Selma kept her alive with three healing spells in a row. Nereth cast darkness over the lair entrance, which confused the dragon for a round. Mara shot out its eye (nat 20!). Esk collapsed the tunnel behind us. Everyone survived. Nobody at the table can believe it. The egg is in Tovin's pack and it is warm. Afterward we spent twenty real minutes debating whether to sell the egg, hatch it, or return it, and did not come to an agreement. Selma is out of spell slots, Brakka is at 4 HP, and Mara's player will not stop talking about the nat 20.

Running the inn arc. Erin (PC) took over the Wandering Inn this week after the old owner vanished. First she cleaned it top to bottom, which took two days. Then she cooked a stew for the goblins that kept hanging around outside instead of chasing them off, and they came back the next night with a dead rabbit as payment. Relc (NPC guard) came by to shake her down for a 'permit fee' and she argued him out of it. On the fourth day a pack of Shield Spiders came up the hill and she held the door with a frying pan and a pot of boiling oil until Relc came back with other guards. By the end of the week she'd served thirty meals, had two regular customers, and one goblin was helping her wash dishes. Relc says the Watch captain wants to meet her, which could be good or bad. The goblins keep leaving little gifts by the door now, mostly rocks and one very confused chicken.

Session 30!! Milestone. Summary for the group chat: 1) We finally confronted Lady Voss at the opera. Ilse called her out publicly in the middle of the second act, and between the ledgers and Tovin's stolen letters the audience turned on her. 2) Voss's bodyguard, a masked duelist, attacked Ilse. Hadrik stepped in and dueled him on the stage in front of 400 people; it went nine rounds and Hadrik won with a disarm into a riposte. Liora improvised music to it, which the crowd thought was part of the show. 3) Voss fled through the backstage. Tamsin chased her across the rigging and cut the rope that dropped the curtain on her. 4) The Watch arrived and took Voss. Jesk gave a statement and managed to keep everyone else out of jail. 5) Afterward Wick got drunk and tried to sell Voss's opera box to three different people, successfully.
